svg.title: Differential parallax of a Venus transit
svg.desc: Two stations see Venus shifted by different amounts against the Sun. The measured disagreement is the differential parallax, not the solar parallax. About 23 arcseconds is the illustrative shift for a side-on baseline of one Earth radius. Stations can be farther apart, up to about a diameter. Angles are exaggerated. This is not a 1769 measurement.
svg.text: Schematic. Angles exaggerated. Not a traced 1769 track.
Differential parallax is about (1/0.277 - 1) times the solar parallax, about 2.61 times it.
One Earth radius, side-on, is about 23 arcseconds if the solar parallax is the modern 8.79.
That length is an illustration, not a ceiling. Stations can stand up to about a diameter apart.
Halley compared full internal-contact durations. One contact, timed in absolute time, needs longitude.
The black drop is mostly blur and the Sun's dim limb, not Venus's air by itself.
